reasoningContent:
Now write the implementation. Spec: lowercase, split on whitespace, separate . , ! ? from words, drop empty, keep numbers intact.

Implementation: use re to split on whitespace or punctuation, or translate punctuation into tokens.

Approach: re.split(r'([.,!?])|(\s+)', ...) — simpler: tokens = re.findall(r'[^\s.,!?]+|[.,!?]', text.lower()). This splits into runs of non-whitespace-non-punctuation chars, or single punctuation marks. Empty tokens never produced. Numbers intact. "x=1" -> ["x=1"] since = not separator. Good.

Note: lowercase should be applied — spec says return lowercase tokens; lowercase applied to whole text is fine (punctuation unaffected). Edge: Unicode case folding could produce whitespace? Unlikely. But could use str.lower.

Write it.

import re

# Keywords: lowercase tokens, whitespace splitting, `.` `,` `!` `?` as their own
# tokens, no empty tokens, numbers kept intact (see spec.md).
_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[^\s.,!?]+|[.,!?]")


def tokenize(text):
    """Split text into lowercase tokens following the contract in spec.md."""
    return _TOKEN_RE.findall(text.lower())
